title: Bulgogi
subtitle: korean marinated grilled beef
excerpt: Bulgogi is thinly sliced beef marinated in soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and Asian pear, then grilled or pan-fried until caramelised. It is one of Korea's most popular dishes. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Bulgogi, meaning 'fire meat', has roots in the Goguryeo era of Korean history. The marinade style using pear or kiwi as a tenderiser is a classic Korean technique.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the raw marinated beef flat in a bag for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before cooking.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half before cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight in the fridge for deeper flavour.

glossaryTerms.definition: A seasoned liquid mixture used to soak meat or vegetables before cooking. It flavours the food and, in some cases, helps tenderise it.

content.text: Bulgogi uses very thin slices of beef soaked in a sweet and savoury
before hitting a hot pan or grill. The sugars in the marinade help the meat caramelise quickly. Serves 4.
The key is to slice the beef as thinly as possible. Partially freezing the meat for 30 minutes makes this much easier. Ask your butcher to slice it on a machine if available.
Combine all marinade ingredients in a large bowl and stir until the sugar dissolves. Add the
Add the sliced beef, onion, and spring onion to the marinade. Mix well with your hands, making sure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Remove the beef from the fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Heat a large frying pan or griddle over very high heat. Add the vegetable oil.

Cook the beef in batches, spreading it out in a single layer. Do not overcrowd the pan or the meat will steam rather than caramelise. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until the edges are charred and the meat is cooked through.
Transfer to a serving plate and scatter sesame seeds over the top. Serve immediately with steamed rice and kimchi on the side.

attrs.issue: Meat is steaming rather than caramelising
attrs.fix: The pan is not hot enough or the pan is overcrowded. Cook in smaller batches and make sure the pan is smoking before adding the meat.
The slices are too thick. Aim for 3 mm or thinner. Partially freeze the beef for 20 to 30 minutes before slicing to make it easier.
Reduce the soy sauce by 1 tablespoon and taste before adding the beef. Different soy sauce brands vary significantly in saltiness.

content.text: Bulgogi is one of the most well-known Korean dishes outside Korea. It is served at home and in restaurants. Traditionally it was cooked over charcoal on a domed grill at the table. Today most home cooks use a regular frying pan or a ridged griddle. It goes well with rice, lettuce wraps, and banchan side dishes.
